clue.text: After part of summer exercises knocked back sweet drink

indicators.note: after tells us the exercise letters come behind the month in the answer

parts.note: JUL is the short form of July, a summer month

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters for exercises are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercises

explanation.surface: After a summer workout, someone downs a sweet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking, matching the surface, but it reverses PE to EP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint-flavoured bourbon cocktail sweetened with syrup is a classic sugary beverage.

clue.text: Fantastic creature from book featuring in short sweet sentence

indicators.note: featuring in means the book letter appears inside the shortened sweet
short means the final letter of the sweet is cut off

parts.note: a jujube is a chewy fruit-flavoured sweet like a wine gum
bird, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time, is a prison term

explanation.surface: A fantasy beast from a book appears in a brief, sweet sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The creature is from Lewis Carroll's verse. BIRD, from rhyming slang 'bird-lime' (time), is British slang for a jail term; JUJUBE is a gummy sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's imaginary bird, to be shunned in Jabberwocky, is a fantasy beast.

clue.text: Her refrain is endless

definitions.note: the pronoun stands for any woman, so a woman's name can replace it

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for refrain is dropped

parts.note: a lilt is a light, rhythmic tune or song

explanation.surface: Her chorus goes on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet form of Lillian, a woman's name, so a female who could be called 'her'.

clue.text: Magistrate passing death sentence when one's expected cheek to be turned

indicators.note: to be turned means both pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: ETA, estimated time of arrival, is when someone is expected
lip means cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: The judge who condemned the man who taught people to turn the other cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' recalls Jesus' 'turn the other cheek'; here it reverses ETA + LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman governor of Judaea sentenced Jesus to crucifixion, a judge imposing capital punishment.

clue.text: Rugby players eating left pasty for Australian winger

indicators.note: eating means the rugby players take another letter inside them

parts.note: the backs are the rugby players lined up behind the scrum
pasty as an adjective means pale-faced, as does wan

explanation.surface: Rugby backs munch a pasty in place of their Australian wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like the meat pie but is the adjective meaning pale; 'winger' sounds like a rugby wing but is a bird, the black swan native to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-plumaged swan of Australia is a bird, so a winged creature from there.

clue.text: Make tea, put in half of said measure, and stir once

indicators.note: put in means the half-word goes inside the word for making tea

parts.note: to brew is to make tea

indicators.note: half of means only the second pair of the word said is used

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure of about 45 inches

explanation.surface: Tea instructions: brew, add half the measure, and stir once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is slang for prison; the original London Bridewell was a house of correction whose name passed to other jails.
explanation.definitionFit: The London house of correction lent its name to old lock-ups, so a former jail.

clue.text: Italian craftsmen provide a service cutting poles

indicators.note: cutting means the poles are cut out of the word for service

parts.note: matins is the early morning church service

explanation.walkthrough: 'Provide' is a link; 'poles' look like wooden posts but are N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cremona family of violin makers were Italian instrument builders.

clue.text: Time to abandon awfully puny ketch that holed

definitions.note: the clue words describe a thing that punched holes, so they stand for a machine

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled
to abandon means the time letter leaves the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Time to abandon ship: the tiny ketch has been holed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges PUNY KETCH and 'to abandon' takes its T away, a composite anagram. The definition is a machine that punched holes in data cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard device that punched holes in cards for early computers was a hole-making machine.

clue.text: Monument with heraldic surrounds lifted me

indicators.note: surrounds means the heraldic word encloses the other piece

parts.note: armorial means relating to coats of arms, heraldry

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A monument with heraldic borders raised my spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph honouring the fallen of a conflict is a commemorative monument.

clue.text: Architect making centres of Greenwich and Southwark identical?

indicators.note: centres of picks the middle letter of each London district name

parts.note: as means equally or the same, as in 'as good as'

indicators.note: and carries the centre-taking on to the second district name

explanation.surface: An architect who makes the hearts of two London districts look the same.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenwich and Southwark are London boroughs; John Nash designed Regent Street. Making the centres identical is saying N as H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Regency designer of Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion was a celebrated British architect.

clue.text: Musical instrument has mere ring similar in sound

indicators.note: ring as a verb means encircle, so the lake surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a mere is a lake, and Bala (Llyn Tegid) is the largest natural lake in Wales

indicators.note: in sound means the word for similar is given by how it is said, respelt

parts.note: similar means alike

explanation.surface: A musical instrument whose tone is said to be much like a plain bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' is a link. BALA, a Welsh lake, rings ALAIK, a respelling that is said like ALIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular three-stringed Russian lute is one example of a stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: Lots of material belonging to investigators

definitions.meaning: cloth is sold by length, so plenty of fabric is many three-foot lengths
Scotland Yard is the London police detective headquarters; its possessive form means owned by the detectives

explanation.surface: Plenty of fabric is owned by the detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the possessive of the Yard, the Metropolitan Police detectives, with the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth is measured in three-foot units, and the London police headquarters' possessive gives the detectives' ownership.

clue.text: A competent secretary will be often refreshed?

definitions.meaning: a good secretary is capable of taking the minutes of a meeting, equal to them
constantly updated, kept current and fresh

explanation.surface: An efficient secretary will need frequent breaks for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means current or latest, and read literally says capable of handling the minutes, a secretary's record of a meeting.

clue.text: Promote lie, spinning line that's illusion

indicators.note: spinning means the letters whirl round into a new order

explanation.surface: Push a lie, spin a line: it is all an illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like spin-doctoring, with 'spinning' seeming to describe the lie.
explanation.definitionFit: The painting technique, French for 'deceive the eye', creates an optical deception of depth.

clue.text: Corrupt, having no time for children, note

te (or ti) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A corrupt person who has no time for children, take note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link; 'no time for children' reads as a period for grown-ups only, ADULT ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase something by adding impurities is to spoil it, so a verb meaning make impure.

clue.text: Sack that may be packed for a journey

definitions.meaning: to sack someone is to dismiss them, give them the push

definitions.text: that may be packed for a journey
definitions.meaning: the luggage compartment of a car is loaded before a trip

explanation.surface: A bag that a traveller fills before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone is to kick them out, and a car's rear luggage space is filled before a trip.

clue.text: People apparently let out on the street

definitions.text: People apparently let out on the street

parts.words: People apparently let out on the street

clue.text: Maiden in voice on vacation rouses Quakers

clue.text: Loot to keep in flimsy wrapping

parts.note: swag is a burglar's loot
flimsy means thin

explanation.surface: Stolen goods to be hidden inside a flimsy wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Binding round in bands of cloth, as with bandages, is a kind of enveloping.

clue.text: Eastern worker lap dancing: she performs online

indicators.note: dancing means the letters jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: An Eastern worker turns to lap dancing; she performs on a webcam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online' suggests the internet, matching the seedy surface, but means on a line: a tightrope.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus funambulist balances on a stretched cord, so she literally works on a line.

clue.text: Old weapon with a star at its top?

definitions.meaning: a hooked blade on a long staff, a medieval foot soldier's arm

definitions.text: with a star at its top
definitions.meaning: a theatre poster names its leading performer first, at the head

explanation.surface: An antique weapon topped with a star-shaped ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval hooked blade on a pole was an infantry arm, and a theatre poster puts the lead performer first.

clue.text: Material in plaster causes pain, above all

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the pain word on top of the next

parts.note: gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'
sum means the whole amount, all

explanation.surface: Something in a plaster cast gives you pain more than anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Causes' is a link; 'above all' looks like 'especially' but splits into a position word and a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster of Paris is made by heating this soft calcium sulphate mineral, a builder's raw ingredient.

clue.text: One exhorted to blow so-called A-bomb up? Not at all

parts.note: the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima in 1945 was code-named after a small lad
if you are not up at all you are down, that is depressed or sad

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' suggests an explosion but means sounding a horn: the nursery-rhyme shepherd boy is told to come and blow his.

by means times, as in four by three for multiplication

clue.text: Vowel to disappear, say another "I"

parts.note: E is one of the five vowels

explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for the first-person pronoun, one's conscious self.
